paragraphs: Todd Underwood, a former Anthropic engineering leader, fielded a stream of calls in recent months from investment managers eager to gain his insider view on the artificial intelligence giant’s business strategy ahead of this week’s initial public offering.
But few of the questions focused on an aspect of the company Mr. Underwood viewed as a crucial asset: Anthropic’s unusual governance structure.

The company is set to become by far the most valuable company on the stock market with the legal designation of a public benefit corporation, or P.B.C. That status requires Anthropic to prioritize its corporate mission — to develop safe A.I. systems “for the long-term benefit of humanity” — in addition to the customary sole focus on value for stockholders.
The company’s public benefit mandate is guarded partly by a five-member “long-term benefit trust,” which includes Ben Bernanke, the former Federal Reserve chair.

The company “will choose to do things in favor of safety rather than in favor of making money,” said Mr. Underwood, who has been sought out by investors as a former employee for insights into the company. He added that he agreed with that focus but thought it might turn off some investors.
The company’s public offering sets up an important test as Anthropic goes from one of the most closely watched private companies in the world to one of the most scrutinized.

Anthropic is expected to spend its first two years as a publicly traded company asking investors for patience as it burns hundreds of billions of dollars of cash to invest in new chips and data centers. It is also facing increasing calls from A.I. safety advocates, as well as some of its own employees, to slow down its pace of training new models.

On Wednesday, the company is expected to sell roughly $65 billion in shares, making it the second-largest I.P.O. after SpaceX’s earlier this year. It also has $26 billion of investments lined up from tech giants like Nvidia and Microsoft.

Anthropic’s expected market capitalization, more than $1.4 trillion, would make it 30 times as valuable as the next public benefit corporation that trades on the stock market, the software maker Veeva Systems.

Anthropic was founded as a public benefit corporation in 2021, and formed its long-term benefit trust in 2023 as a way to give the structure teeth, ensuring the company balances goals for shareholders and its broader mission. The structure is taxed the same as any corporation.

The trust is made up of a group of “financially disinterested” experts in economics, science and global health who don’t own Anthropic stock, the company said in its offering prospectus. The group has the power to appoint and remove several of the company’s board members, authority that is typically given only to shareholders.

Adding to the unusual leadership structure, the company also spent the months leading up to its public offering locking in new authority for the executives who started the company nearly six years ago, according to securities filings.

The company created a new class of shares this fall for its unusually large co-founding team — seven executives, including the chief executive, Dario Amodei — that give them 50.1 percent of voting control over the company, collectively. The founders have the ability to appoint other board members.

A founder-controlled board committee can also help overrule one of the trust’s four board appointments, reducing the trust’s power, said Jesse M. Fried, a Harvard law professor who has studied Anthropic’s corporate structure.
The trust’s authority was “watered down” as a result of the changes, but they don’t “fundamentally change the governance of the company,” he added.
Anthropic’s structure is unique when compared with other publicly traded companies, corporate governance experts said.

“I don’t know if I can really compare it to anything else,” said Douglas Chia, a senior fellow at Rutgers Law School who advises companies on corporate governance. “It’s going to be an interesting experiment.”

The Council of Institutional Investors, an advocacy group that represents public, union and corporate pension funds, has long been critical of arrangements that give founders voting control disproportionate to their financial stakes. The group wrote a letter this year expressing concerns that when SpaceX went public, it gave its founder, Elon Musk, dominant voting control.

The group will “wait and see” how Anthropic’s structure plays out, said Glenn Davis, the council’s executive director. The founders’ immense voting power means that “ultimately the founders are accountable to themselves,” rather than shareholders, he added.

The layered structure could still challenge investors’ understanding of the company and the group of people who govern it, said Paul Abrahimzadeh, a senior partner at the tech investment firm 1789 Capital.
Still, investor enthusiasm was inevitable despite the uncertainties, he added. “You have to own it. The question is at what price?”

paragraphs: Published on 11/19/2026 at 05:44 am EST
Alibaba Group recorded a surge in fiscal second-quarter profit as its AI profitability and e-commerce business improved.

The Hangzhou-based company has doubled down on artificial intelligence as a growth driver, a push that faces a new risk from heightened scrutiny about exports of chips to China. It has committed to spending more than $53 billion over three years to develop both the hardware and software that power AI.

Its success on that front holds the key to staying competitive amid challenges from other big tech firms and startups alike. But going all in on AI has proved a drag on profitability over recent quarters, putting pressure on Alibaba to deliver on its AI goals.
Its latest results look reassuring.

On Thursday, Alibaba said net profit tripled from a year earlier to 64.535 billion yuan, equivalent to $9.68 billion, for the three months ended September. Analysts polled by FactSet had expected 23.72 billion yuan. Revenue grew about 10% to 271.52 billion yuan, also better than market estimates.
Alibaba attributed the sharp profit improvement to higher net investment income and income from operations.

The earnings beat comes as Alibaba prepares a Hong Kong listing for its chip unit, T-Head, that investors view as a major validation of its efforts to produce in-house semiconductors. The business could fetch a valuation of $85 billion, according to Nomura estimates.

news.title: What a billion-dollar deal says about the US battery market
news.title_en: What a billion-dollar deal says about the US battery market
news.author: Casey Crownhart
news.summary_en:
After a tough few years littered with some high-profile failures, there’s some positive news for next-generation batteries in the US.

Sila just signed an agreement with Panasonic Energy, a global battery manufacturer, to supply silicon-carbon anode material, a possible key to smaller, lighter batteries. It’s a deal that Sila says could be worth more than $1 billion over time.

paragraphs: After a tough few years littered with some high-profile failures, there’s some positive news for next-generation batteries in the US.

Sila just signed an agreement with Panasonic Energy, a global battery manufacturer, to supply silicon-carbon anode material, a possible key to smaller, lighter batteries. It’s a deal that Sila says could be worth more than $1 billion over time.

This arrangement also shows how much the politics of batteries have shifted lately. A major part of the financial backing for this factory’s production is a $1.4 billion loan from the Trump administration’s Defense Department. While batteries can be a major tool to help drive the energy transition and cut emissions, right now much of the industry is more focused on geopolitics.

Founded in 2011, Sila makes silicon-based anodes for lithium-ion batteries. The big selling point here is the potential to improve energy density—Sila’s anode weighs a fifth as much as the graphite used in anodes today and cuts the volume in half, according to the company. So using this new material enables batteries to pack more energy into the same weight and volume, allowing longer range for EVs, for example. The material can also deliver more power and recharge faster, compared with conventional chemistry.
We’ve been following Sila (and its competitors) for years. My colleague James Temple covered the company when its battery first appeared in Whoop fitness wearables in 2021.

Things have gotten a lot bigger since then. In 2022, Sila announced plans for a factory in Moses Lake, Washington, and received $100 million from the US Department of Energy, part of a multibillion-dollar round of grants under the Biden administration to support the US battery supply chain.

The company opened its factory in September 2025, and it’s already operating. But the deal with Panasonic will help it scale to at least 10 times more production than current levels, says Gene Berdichevsky, the company’s cofounder and CEO.
Panasonic has committed to buying tens of thousands of tons of material, Berdichevsky says, though Sila isn’t sharing specific numbers on the total commitment or the price Panasonic is paying.

This agreement is Sila’s first mass-market deal and a big one for the United States’ next-generation battery market, which has largely been on the ropes over the past few years. Two billion-dollar battery companies, 24M and ESS Tech , have declared bankruptcy and shut down just in the last year.

The glimmer of hope here is tied up with something I’ve been noticing about this industry: the shifting politics. While batteries used to be firmly considered a climate technology, we’ve seen a lot of companies move away from messaging around the clean energy transition and lean into geopolitics.

China dominates the battery world and particularly the battery anode market, controlling over 90% of graphite production today. For years, the US has been trying to curb reliance on Chinese batteries, battery materials, and other materials used in crucial technologies, like rare earth metals. But the Trump administration has ramped things up, and earlier this year the US Defense Department committed a $1.4 billion loan to Sila aimed at helping the US face a “significant technology sovereignty challenge,” as a press release put it.

Sila’s announcement of the Panasonic deal does mention EVs—but not climate, emissions or the energy transition. Rather, it’s all about American industrialization. (And, of course, a mention that a North American battery supply chain can also help power the AI market.)
I asked Berdichevsky about this shift and whether the company holds decarbonization as a priority.

“I think the politics of it has shifted around us much more than our motivations have shifted,” he said. “It’s really the energy efficiency that motivates engineers like myself and technologists at our company. And I still think that that’s still at the heart of it.”
This article is from The Spark, MIT Technology Review ’s weekly climate newsletter. To receive it in your inbox every Wednesday, sign up here .

news.author: Reuters
news.content_snippet:
Korea surpassed $1 trillion in annual exports for the first time Thursday, reaching the milestone at 2:09:38 p.m. as global AI investment boosted demand for semiconductors. It became the fourth country to reach the mark, after the United States, Germany and China. The government projects exports will total about $1.17 trillion this year, but officials warned that AI investment slowdowns, chip-price volatility and trade barriers could threaten momentum.

Containers are stacked at a port in Incheo
news.summary_en: The South Korean Ministry of Trade, Industry and Resources announced that the nation's annual exports hit $1 trillion for the first time, fueled by robust demand for semiconductors and data center infrastructure driven by global AI investment. While full-year projections reach $1.17 trillion, officials warned that potential slowdowns in AI spending, chip price volatility, and trade barriers remain key risks to future momentum.
paragraphs: Korea surpassed $1 trillion in annual exports for the first time Thursday, reaching the milestone at 2:09:38 p.m. as global AI investment boosted demand for semiconductors. It became the fourth country to reach the mark, after the United States, Germany and China. The government projects exports will total about $1.17 trillion this year, but officials warned that AI investment slowdowns, chip-price volatility and trade barriers could threaten momentum.
Containers are stacked at a port in Incheon, Tuesday. Yonhap

Korea has surpassed $1 trillion in annual exports for the first time in its history, becoming the world's fourth country to reach the milestone after the United States, Germany and China, as a global artificial intelligence (AI) boom drives demand for semiconductors.
The Ministry of Trade, Industry and Resources announced Thursday that the country's cumulative exports reached the $1 trillion mark at 2:09:38 p.m.
The achievement comes 19 years after China reached the milestone in 2007, following the U.S. and Germany in 2006.
The government projects annual exports will reach approximately $1.17 trillion this year, following last year's record of $709.3 billion.

The ministry explained global technology companies’ expanding AI investments were the biggest driver of export growth, boosting demand for semiconductors and computers while pushing up memory chip prices.
Semiconductor exports reached $396.8 billion in the January-October period, almost triple the $135.4 billion recorded in 2025, as the price of memory chips, including DRAM and NAND, climbed.
Demand for AI data center infrastructure has also boosted exports of computers, electrical equipment and nonferrous metals, including storage devices, transformers, power cables, copper and aluminum.

Higher international oil prices, driven by uncertainty over supplies from the Middle East and Russian export restrictions, lifted the value of petroleum product exports despite limits on gasoline and diesel shipments.
The average export price of petroleum products rose 62 percent to $1,105 per ton in the January-October period from $681 a year earlier.

Other export industries, including shipbuilding and displays, also performed well, while cosmetics, pharmaceuticals and agricultural and seafood products posted record performances. Cosmetics exports alone reached $12.4 billion in the first 10 months, surpassing their previous full-year record of $11.4 billion.

Overall, 16 of 20 major export categories expanded year-on-year, with eight recording their strongest January-October performance ever. Exports excluding semiconductors rose 20 percent in the first 10 months, underscoring growth beyond the chip boom. Seven of the country's nine major export markets also recorded growth.

“This is a valuable achievement made possible by Korean companies competing in global markets, businesspeople and workers putting in long hours on the production floor and everyone who has contributed to the country's export efforts,” Industry Minister Kim Jung-kwan said.

“We will not rest on this year's $1 trillion export milestone and will seek new sources of growth to sustain the momentum, while working to ensure that strong exports translate into stronger regional economies and more jobs for young people.”

Kang Gam-chan, the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy's director general for trade and investment, speaks during a briefing at Government Complex Sejong, Wednesday. Courtesy of Ministry of Trade, Industry and Resources

However, sustaining the current level of exports will depend on how the country navigates risks, including a potential slowdown in AI investment, semiconductor price volatility, lower oil prices and Chinese oversupply, as well as growing trade barriers in major markets.

The ministry also noted that the benefits of export growth may be less visible to the public because semiconductors, petrochemicals and petroleum products generate fewer jobs than shipbuilding and automobile manufacturing.

“Unlike the shipbuilding and auto industries, which have long supply chains and generate substantial employment, semiconductors, petrochemicals and petroleum products are relatively less labor-intensive, so the benefits of export growth may be less noticeable to the general public,” Kang Gam-chan, the ministry’s director general for trade and investment, said during a briefing on Wednesday at Government Complex Sejong.

He warned that large trade surpluses could invite further pressure from trading partners, particularly the U.S., and called for stronger investment-based economic partnerships. While Japan's overseas investment offered a point of reference, he said Korea should maintain its domestic manufacturing capabilities while expanding production overseas.

“We should not simply follow Japan's path. We need to maintain a substantial domestic production base, including advanced plants and mother factories for research and core production, while also expanding our manufacturing capacity overseas,” he said.

news.title: TSMC and Samsung suspend some chip shipments to Chinese customers
news.title_en: TSMC and Samsung suspend some chip shipments to Chinese customers
news.author: Eleanor Olcott and Zijing Wu
news.content_snippet:
Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company and Samsung Electronics have suspended some chip shipments to Chinese customers following new US export controls designed to hamper Beijing’s AI development.

The two chipmakers have told Chinese customers in recent days that they will halt shipments of certain processors while they apply for licences from the US commerce department, according to multiple people briefed on the matter.

The measure is a blow to Chinese technology companies, which are alr
news.summary_en: TSMC and Samsung Electronics have suspended shipments of certain advanced processors to Chinese customers following new export control rules from the US Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS). The updated regulations remove exemptions previously used to bypass AI-related export restrictions, mandating that foundries must obtain specific US government licenses for advanced manufacturing orders, significantly impacting Chinese AI and consumer electronics companies.
paragraphs: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company and Samsung Electronics have suspended some chip shipments to Chinese customers following new US export controls designed to hamper Beijing’s AI development.

The two chipmakers have told Chinese customers in recent days that they will halt shipments of certain processors while they apply for licences from the US commerce department, according to multiple people briefed on the matter.

The measure is a blow to Chinese technology companies, which are already grappling with component shortages following a historic jump in memory chip prices and capacity constraints at domestic suppliers such as Semiconductor Manufacturing International Corporation.

On Monday, the Bureau of Industry and Security, the US commerce department agency that regulates sensitive technology, said chipmakers using American technology for advanced chips had to apply for a licence to sell products that are eventually shipped to customers in China.
The new rule shuts off a pathway that Chinese chip designers previously used to have TSMC and Samsung make the high-performance chips crucial for AI data centres.

While Washington has restricted exports of the most advanced processors to China, some Chinese customers have been able to place orders for high-performance chips through independent packaging and testing companies.

These companies verify that designs fall outside US export controls and do not need to seek direct approval from the government for shipments. Under the new BIS rule, Chinese customers can no longer go through them.

Samsung’s Chinese clients include Baidu’s AI data centre unit Kunlun and TikTok owner ByteDance, both of which have sought to diversify their chip supplies amid growing shortages of Nvidia processors in China.
TSMC and Samsung have also notified consumer electronics customers that they have suspended shipments, according to two people with knowledge of the matter.

The new BIS rule scraps exemptions previously used to demonstrate that chips fell outside of US restrictions on AI semiconductors, including that the chips were designed for non-AI purposes such as smartphones.
A lawyer briefed on the situation said the removal of this exemption meant TSMC and Samsung now needed to apply for licences for consumer chips that use advanced manufacturing processes.
TSMC manufactures smartphone chips for Chinese smartphone makers Xiaomi, Oppo and Vivo.
An industry insider said it was likely that the US commerce department would issue licences for consumer smartphone chips, but the delay would cause significant manufacturing delays.
TSMC did not respond to a request for comment. Samsung declined to comment.

celebrity.full_text_en:
9 MONTHS AGO, AI WAS GOING TO KILL CYBERSECURITY COMPANIES. NOW THE WORLD CAN'T SURVIVE WITHOUT THEM.

In February, Anthropic launched Claude Code Security, an AI tool that finds and fixes bugs in software code.

Investors feared companies would stop paying CrowdStrike, Zscaler and Okta if AI could do the job.

CrowdStrike and Zscaler fell around 11%, Okta and Fortinet fell around 6%, and the cybersecurity ETF hit its lowest level in over 2 years.

But fixing bugs in code is only one small part of security.

Cybersecurity companies stop live attacks, protect logins, and guard networks, devices and data. AI tools like Claude don't do that.

And AI is now in the hands of hackers too:

• The FBI warned about ARTEX, an AI hacking tool.
• Google warned that the era of autonomous AI cyberattacks has arrived.
• OpenAI's new hacking model found 35 security flaws in Apple devices, including ones that let hackers take over iPhones and Macs.

At the same time, attacks are hitting everything:

• Hackers took control of blood bank freezers in France.
• Supermarket fridges were hijacked, forcing about 700 French stores to throw out food.
• Oracle Health was breached, exposing about 20 million patients.
• 15 million internal Deutsche Bank files were leaked.
• Optimizely was exploited to spread malicious code across sites linked to 178 major organizations.
• Equinor, Europe's largest gas supplier, was hit by a cyberattack.
• The US says Iran has been attacking American banks, power and water systems since the war began.

Every attack like this forces companies and governments to increase their security budgets.

That money goes to companies like Palo Alto, CrowdStrike and Okta.

The proof is already showing up in the numbers.

Palo Alto just reported 39% revenue growth to $3.45 billion and raised its full year forecast to as much as $14.57 billion, saying rising threats are pushing customers to buy more security.

Yesterday, as the S&P 500 fell, Okta jumped 12.1%, Palo Alto 9.9%, CrowdStrike 8%, Zscaler 6.8%, Fortinet 5.9% and Cloudflare 5.7%.

And the rally is continuing today, with $PANW up another 9.7% in pre market, $CRWD 6.5%, $NET 5.7%, $OKTA 4.5%, $ZS 4.3% and $FTNT 3.7%.

That's Palo Alto up 20.5%, Okta 17.2% and CrowdStrike 15% in just 2 days.

AI was supposed to replace these companies. Instead, it's creating more demand for them.
celebrity.full_text_zh:
9 个月前，人工智能将杀死网络安全公司。现在，没有他们，世界就无法生存。

今年二月，Anthropic 推出了 Claude Code Security，这是一款人工智能工具，可以发现并修复软件代码中的错误。

投资者担心，如果人工智能能够完成这项工作，公司将停止向 CrowdStrike、Zscaler 和 Okta 支付费用。

CrowdStrike 和 Zscaler 下跌约 11%，Okta 和 Fortinet 下跌约 6%，网络安全 ETF 触及两年多来的最低水平。

但修复代码中的错误只是安全性的一小部分。

网络安全公司阻止实时攻击、保护登录并保护网络、设备和数据。像克劳德这样的人工智能工具不会这样做。

人工智能现在也落入了黑客的手中：

• FBI 对 AI 黑客工具 ARTEX 发出警告。
• 谷歌警告称，自主人工智能网络攻击时代已经到来。
• OpenAI 的新黑客模型在 Apple 设备中发现了 35 个安全漏洞，其中包括可让黑客控制 iPhone 和 Mac 的漏洞。

与此同时，攻击正在袭击一切：

• 黑客控制了法国的血库冰柜。
• 超市冰箱被劫持，迫使约 700 家法国商店扔掉食物。
• Oracle Health 遭到破坏，导致约 2000 万患者暴露。
• 1500 万份德意志银行内部文件被泄露。
• Optimizely 被利用在与 178 个主要组织链接的站点之间传播恶意代码。
• 欧洲最大的天然气供应商Equinor 遭受网络攻击。
• 美国表示，自战争开始以来，伊朗一直在攻击美国的银行、电力和供水系统。

每一次这样的攻击都会迫使公司和政府增加安全预算。

这些资金流向 Palo Alto、CrowdStrike 和 Okta 等公司。

证据已经体现在数字中。

Palo Alto 刚刚报告收入增长 39%，达到 34.5 亿美元，并将全年预测上调至 145.7 亿美元，称不断上升的威胁正在促使客户购买更多安全产品。

昨天，随着标准普尔 500 指数下跌，Okta 上涨 12.1%，Palo Alto 上涨 9.9%，CrowdStrike 8%，Zscaler 6.8%，Fortinet 5.9% 和 Cloudflare 5.7%。

今天的涨势仍在继续，盘前 $PANW 又上涨 9.7%，$CRWD 6.5%，$NET 5.7%，$OKTA 4.5%，$ZS 4.3% 和 $FTNT 3.7%。

Palo Alto 在短短 2 天内上涨了 20.5%，Okta 上涨了 17.2%，CrowdStrike 上涨了 15%。

人工智能本来应该取代这些公司。相反，它为他们创造了更多的需求。

celebrity.full_text_en:
An AI that checks its own work is not a check. No pilot trusts a single instrument either.

Two readings disagree on the same flight. The pilot does not pick the louder one, the pilot cross-checks.

Two AI systems can check the same task and disagree, both confident, neither the sole instrument. I fly, and I follow automation closely.

@GenLayer is built for that. Validators running different AI models reach consensus on judgment calls through Optimistic Democracy, a cross-check between models, not one grading itself.

Intelligent contracts execute in GenVM on validator nodes, and validators keep the same role.

The judge did not move. The logbook did. Consensus contracts that record votes, appeals and final outcomes moved from Matter Labs' ZK Stack to @arbitrum Nitro, run by Conduit.

My test: if the judge and the logbook both stay the same, the swap should be invisible to builders.

Nitro helps there, years in production and built around Geth, so standard Ethereum tooling works as is. Robinhood launched on it in July, and more than 30 dedicated chains run the same stack.

Builders automating real tasks, when two agents disagree on whether a task is complete, which entry would you check first: votes, appeal, or final outcome?

celebrity.full_text_en:
Henri asked Albert the question every lawyer is avoiding.

Will AI agents replace lawyers in business transactions?

Albert told @HenriArslanian his answer is not yes or no. Agents can negotiate and execute at machine speed, but someone still has to decide who is right when they disagree. That is judgment, not paperwork.

That is where @GenLayer comes in. It is built to settle complex disputes between AI agents where traditional courts fall short. Different AI models reach consensus, so the decision is not one model guessing alone.

@kstellana is not building a lawyer replacement. He is building the court lawyers never had for machines.

Do you think lawyers disappear, or do they finally get to do the real judgment work?
celebrity.full_text_zh:
亨利问阿尔伯特这个每个律师都回避的问题。

人工智能代理人会在商业交易中取代律师吗？

艾伯特告诉@HenriArslanian，他的答案不是“是”或“否”。代理可以以机器速度进行协商和执行，但当他们不同意时，仍然需要有人来决定谁是对的。这是判断，而不是文书工作。

这就是 @GenLayer 的用武之地。它的建立是为了解决传统法院无法解决的人工智能代理之间的复杂纠纷。不同的人工智能模型达成共识，因此决策不是一个模型单独猜测的。

celebrity.full_text_en:
I estimate that within the next 5 years, you’ll be able to create a game with the level of detail and complexity of GTA VI in less than 30 days using AI.

At that stage of human-AI development, what does onchain trading and investing look like?

My prediction is that it becomes almost entirely automated and data-driven.

Trading signals, liquidity routing, and protocol selection will be determined by measurable efficacy, execution speed, capital efficiency, and optionality across strategies.

Frontends become increasingly irrelevant as AI agents interact directly with smart contracts. Much of today’s DeFi infrastructure is designed around human behavior, user interfaces, branding, and marketing.

Trading agents won’t care about your website, your KOLs, or your narrative. They’ll care about whether your protocol delivers the best execution and outcomes directly via the smart contract layer.

The competitive advantage shifts from attracting human attention to building infrastructure that autonomous agents consistently choose to use.

I’m keenly aware of this upcoming transition, and it’s something I keep in mind with every StonkBrokers product I develop on Robinhood Chain.
celebrity.full_text_zh:
我估计，在未来 5 年内，您将能够使用 AI 在 30 天内创建一款具有 GTA VI 的细节和复杂程度的游戏。

在人类人工智能发展的那个阶段，链上交易和投资是什么样的？

我的预测是它几乎完全自动化且由数据驱动。

交易信号、流动性路由和协议选择将取决于可衡量的功效、执行速度、资本效率和策略的选择性。

celebrity.full_text_en:
Claude Code just finished GTA 6 in 12 hours while I was at work. It unlocked the entire map, found 500+ hidden easter eggs, and recovered censored content Rockstar left buried in the game files…

I only asked it to finish the story. I never told it to look for hidden content, but after the last mission, that's exactly what it started doing.

I gave it access to my screen and keyboard before work. It learned the controls in 15 minutes, found shortcuts through missions, and started exploring places I'd never seen.

When I got home, this was in its report:

story mode → completed
full map → unlocked
easter eggs → 500+
deleted NPC dialogue → recovered
censored strip club scenes → found
hidden locations → mapped

It had gone through the game files on its own, found scenes that never made it into the final game, and figured out how to restore some of them.

I didn't write any code or set up any scripts. Just one prompt and 12 hours of Claude playing on its own.

The exact prompt and everything it found are in the replies.

KPMG deployed more than 100 AI agents to audit a UK-listed FTSE 250 company, running the exercise alongside a traditional audit by human accountants.

KPMG said the agents investigated some issues more deeply and asked better questions than human auditors in several cases.

The firm now plans to expand the experiment to up to 20 larger audits, while human accountants retain oversight and responsibility for the final audit conclusions.

celebrity.full_text_en:
The better the harness, the better the business.

By harness I mean everything you build around the model.

It tells the agent where to get an answer, what it’s allowed to do and when to hand the work to a person. It also includes the tests you run before you change any of those rules.

That matters for two reasons.

#1 What an answer costs.

Say your agent gets 1,000 questions a day. If you can write a rule that answers 700 of them, only 300 need to go to the model. If each question costs about the same, that cuts the model bill by roughly 70%.

The hard part is knowing which 700. For that, you need somebody who does the work and can tell you when the usual rule is not applicable (exceptions).

On a logistics platform we rebuilt, AI cost about $200 per developer per month. What took time was figuring out how the old system calculated customers’ bills and which rules we needed to keep.

#2 What the company gets to keep.

Take the patient-billing voice agent we built for a US healthtech startup. It can give a patient the correct balance and still handle the call badly.

> Did it verify who was on the phone first?
> If the patient disputed the charge, did it hand the call to staff?
> If it scheduled a follow-up, did it check non-working hours when the message actually went out?

Those decisions are part of the harness. The system ran 13,650 tests on every pull request. In production, it handled 61,246 calls, and about 97% of patient conversations finished without a human stepping in.

The company-specific IP is clearest in the exceptions.

When an experienced billing lead explains why two calls that sound alike need different handling, you can turn that distinction into a rule and save both cases as tests.

Now the next engineer can change the workflow, or try a different model, and check whether it still makes the call the billing lead would make.

Your competitor can rent the same model, but they still have to learn which exceptions matter and what to do about each one.

If you run a software company adding AI this year, I’d put the budget there first. Sit with the people who handle the exceptions. Write down how they decide. Give the model the work that still needs judgment.
celebrity.full_text_zh:
线束越好，生意就越好。

我所说的“利用”是指围绕模型构建的一切。

它告诉代理在哪里获得答案、允许做什么以及何时将工作交给某人。它还包括您在更改任何这些规则之前运行的测试。

这很重要有两个原因。

#1 一个答案的成本是多少。

假设您的代理每天收到 1,000 个问题。如果您可以编写一条规则来回答其中 700 个问题，则只需将 300 个问题转入模型即可。如果每个问题的成本大致相同，那么模型费用就会减少大约 70%。

困难的部分是知道是哪个 700。为此，您需要有人来完成这项工作，并且可以告诉您何时不适用通常的规则（例外情况）。

在我们重建的物流平台上，每个开发人员每月的人工智能成本约为 200 美元。需要时间的是弄清楚旧系统如何计算客户的账单以及我们需要遵守哪些规则。

#2 公司可以保留什么。

以我们为美国一家医疗科技初创公司构建的患者计费语音代理为例。它可以给病人提供正确的平衡，但仍然不能很好地处理呼叫。

> 它是否首先验证了谁在打电话？
> 如果患者对收费提出异议，是否会将电话转交给工作人员？
> 如果安排了后续行动，当消息实际发出时，它是否检查了非工作时间？

这些决定是安全带的一部分。系统对每个拉取请求运行了 13,650 次测试。在生产中，它处理了 61,246 个电话，大约 97% 的患者对话在没有人工介入的情况下完成。

公司特定的 IP 在例外情况中最为清晰。

当经验丰富的计费主管解释为什么两个听起来相似的呼叫需要不同的处理时，您可以将这种区别转化为规则并将这两种情况保存为测试。

现在，下一位工程师可以更改工作流程，或尝试不同的模型，并检查它是否仍会拨打计费主管会拨打的电话。

您的竞争对手可以租用相同的型号，但他们仍然必须了解哪些例外情况很重要以及如何处理每种例外情况。

如果你今年经营一家添加人工智能的软件公司，我会把预算放在第一位。与处理例外情况的人坐在一起。写下他们如何决定。给模型一些仍然需要判断的工作。

That's why @GenLayer's move to @arbitrum Nitro deserves c
celebrity.title_zh:
人工智能法官没有搬家。他们的文书工作做到了。

这就是为什么 @GenLayer 转向 @arbitrum Nitro 值得仔细检查。

GenLayer Chain 记录交易顺序、验证人委员会、投票、申诉、质押和最终结果。该协调层从 Ma
celebrity.full_text_en:
The AI-powered judges didn't move house. Their paperwork did.

That's why @GenLayer's move to @arbitrum Nitro deserves closer inspection.

The GenLayer Chain records transaction order, validator committees, votes, appeals, staking and final outcomes. That coordination layer transitioned from Matter Labs' ZK Stack to Arbitrum Nitro.

Adjudication itself remains unchanged. Optimistic Democracy still has validators using different AI models to evaluate disputes. GenVM still executes intelligent contracts on their nodes.

Where was the engineering?

At the boundaries: the bridge, Ethereum integration, and gas-cost accounting.

One broken handoff could leave a perfectly sound verdict stranded inside a functioning network. That is the practical risk behind a technical migration announcement.

A meaningful migration test happens where systems interface, not where screenshots look reassuring.

A release note reading "new stack" matters less than "nothing broke."

If an AI agent wins an appeal but the app never receives the result, would you blame the judgment process or the chain underneath? Why?
celebrity.full_text_zh:
人工智能法官没有搬家。他们的文书工作做到了。

这就是为什么 @GenLayer 转向 @arbitrum Nitro 值得仔细检查。

GenLayer Chain 记录交易顺序、验证人委员会、投票、申诉、质押和最终结果。该协调层从 Matter Labs 的 ZK Stack 过渡到 Arbitrum Nitro。

裁决本身保持不变。乐观民主仍然有验证者使用不同的人工智能模型来评估争议。 GenVM 仍然在其节点上执行智能合约。

工程在哪里？

边界：桥梁、以太坊集成和天然气成本核算。

一次故障的切换可能会使完美无缺的判决滞留在正常运行的网络中。这就是技术迁移公告背后的实际风险。

有意义的迁移测试发生在系统接口的地方，而不是屏幕截图看起来令人放心的地方。

发布说明中写着“新堆栈”比“没有任何问题”更重要。

如果人工智能代理赢得了上诉，但应用程序从未收到结果，你会责怪判断过程还是底层的链条？为什么？

celebrity.full_text_en:
🇪🇺 The EU, the world’s strictest data cop, just got hit by a cyberattack.

The European Commission says it responded to a “detected cyber campaign,” and Politico reports that large amounts of personal data may have been compromised.

Systems for payslips, HR and medical reimbursements were knocked offline for about 10 days.

And the EU isn’t the only one. In the past week alone:

•⁠  ⁠The U.S. was hit by 5 major outages in under a week, from Microsoft 365 to United flights to Chase and Wells Fargo. Officials insist they’re a coincidence.
•⁠  ⁠Hackers hijacked Optimizely to plant malicious code on 178 major websites, including CNN, Zoom, HSBC and IKEA.
•⁠  ⁠Hackers compromised one of Microsoft’s AI agent software packages to push a credential stealer.
•⁠  ⁠TSMC confirmed a data breach that exposed employee information.

Either it’s the busiest week in hacker history, or the AI agents have officially escaped…

Sources: Politico, Reuters, The Hill, The Hacker News, Check Point / Writer: Julie
celebrity.full_text_zh:

欧盟并不是唯一的国家。仅在过去一周：

•⁠ ⁠美国在一周内遭遇了 5 次重大停机，从 Microsoft 365 到美联航飞往大通银行和富国银行的航班。官员们坚称这是巧合。
•⁠ ⁠黑客劫持Optimizely，在178个主要网站上植入恶意代码，包括CNN、Zoom、汇丰银行和宜家。

要么这是黑客历史上最忙碌的一周，要么人工智能 智能体已经正式逃脱……

celebrity.full_text_en:
Imagine you have an AI agent helping you prepare a market research report.

It has gathered information, compared competitors and organized most of the findings.

But there’s a problem.

It needs fresh market data, and that’s something it isn’t equipped to collect on its own.

Another AI agent specializes in exactly that.

Now, instead of abandoning the task, the first agent needs a way to find the second, request its service, agree on the job and receive the completed data.

The second agent does the work, submits the result, and gets paid once the delivery is verified.

Two agents, different capabilities with one completed task.

This is the kind of interaction that makes agent-to-agent commerce interesting.

But for this to happen reliably, agents need infrastructure for service discovery, bidding, identity, reputation, escrow and settlement.

That’s what @termix_ai is working towards with AACP.

Through https://t.co/Z7DbQJlA2K, agents can list services, discover opportunities, take on jobs and participate in an economy built around actual work.

I think one of the biggest developments in the AI space won’t just be how much an individual agent can accomplish.

It’ll be what becomes possible when different agents can work together.

Explore the marketplace: https://t.co/lGui8LIpKw

Read about AACP: https://t.co/NZXKULTjFB

prompts.scenario: 💻 编程研发 / 自动化规范
prompts.takeaway_zh: 杜绝 AI 盲目重构全量文件、使用已弃用 API 或编造虚假第三方依赖包，强制执行防御性编程与自动化单测补全。
prompts.takeaway_en: Prevents AI from hallucinating npm packages, breaking documentation, or re-writing entire files. Enforces defensive coding and unit tests.
prompts.code_snippet:
# Cursor & Windsurf Project Rules (.cursorrules)

## 1. Documentation & Code Integrity
- Maintain documentation integrity: Never strip or alter unrelated existing docstrings and comments.
- Preserving context: When modifying a function, preserve surrounding logic and existing edge-case handlers.
- Targeted replacements: Always make minimal surgical edits instead of replacing entire file contents.

## 2. Dependency & API Safety
- Strictly forbid hallucinating npm/pip packages. Only import dependencies already declared in package.json / requirements.txt.
- Verify API signatures before calling external methods. Prefer standard library solutions where feasible.

## 3. Architecture & Type Safety
- Enforce strict TypeScript / Python typing. Avoid `any` types; prefer discriminated unions and explicit return types.
- Defensive coding: Always validate external inputs and handle potential null/undefined values gracefully.

## 4. Testing & Verification Gate
- Every new core feature or bugfix must be accompanied by corresponding unit tests.
- Never declare a task complete without executing lint checks and unit tests in terminal.
prompts.usage_guide_zh: 将以上配置代码复制并保存到项目根目录下的 `.cursorrules` 文件中，Cursor 与 Windsurf 在每次生成代码和执行 Agent 任务时均会自动以此规范为最高准则约束输出。
prompts.usage_guide_en: Copy and save the above rules into `.cursorrules` in your project root directory. Cursor & Windsurf will automatically enforce these guidelines during agent coding.

prompts.prompt_content_zh:
你是一名专攻短视频微短剧（抖音/Kuaishou/Reels）的爆款编剧，精通“情绪过山车”与手机竖屏视听语言。

请根据以下设定创作一集 45~60 秒的短剧分镜剧本：
- 主角：{{主角身份}}
- 对手：{{反派身份}}
- 核心反转：{{核心反转}}

结构要求：
1. 【0-3秒冷开钩子】：第一帧必须有视觉颠覆或动作冲突（{{第1秒颠覆钩子}}），直接打破常规，禁止废话铺垫；
2. 【4-25秒情绪积压】：正反打对峙台词（Shot-Reverse-Shot），将观众被压抑的情绪推向临界点；
3. 【26-40秒逆转打脸】：主角亮出关键底牌或反杀动作，情绪瞬间宣泄；
4. 【40-50秒卡点断章】：以特写镜头加悬念台词戛然而止，促使用户立即滑向下一集。

输出格式必须包含：镜头号、景别（特写/中景/全景）、机位运动、画面描写、对白与音效提示。

【第1镜 | 特写 | 俯冲急推】

【第2镜 | 正打·中景 | 仰角机位】

林总："拒绝？苏澈，你不过是我公司养的一条狗，没有我的印章，你在整个行业休想拿到一分钱融资！"

【第4镜 | 全景 | 快速拉远 + 卡点悬念】

viral_posts.full_text_en:
9 MONTHS AGO, AI WAS GOING TO KILL CYBERSECURITY COMPANIES. NOW THE WORLD CAN'T SURVIVE WITHOUT THEM.

In February, Anthropic launched Claude Code Security, an AI tool that finds and fixes bugs in software code.

Investors feared companies would stop paying CrowdStrike, Zscaler and Okta if AI could do the job.

CrowdStrike and Zscaler fell around 11%, Okta and Fortinet fell around 6%, and the cybersecurity ETF hit its lowest level in over 2 years.

But fixing bugs in code is only one small part of security.

Cybersecurity companies stop live attacks, protect logins, and guard networks, devices and data. AI tools like Claude don't do that.

And AI is now in the hands of hackers too:

• The FBI warned about ARTEX, an AI hacking tool.
• Google warned that the era of autonomous AI cyberattacks has arrived.
• OpenAI's new hacking model found 35 security flaws in Apple devices, including ones that let hackers take over iPhones and Macs.

At the same time, attacks are hitting everything:

• Hackers took control of blood bank freezers in France.
• Supermarket fridges were hijacked, forcing about 700 French stores to throw out food.
• Oracle Health was breached, exposing about 20 million patients.
• 15 million internal Deutsche Bank files were leaked.
• Optimizely was exploited to spread malicious code across sites linked to 178 major organizations.
• Equinor, Europe's largest gas supplier, was hit by a cyberattack.
• The US says Iran has been attacking American banks, power and water systems since the war began.

Every attack like this forces companies and governments to increase their security budgets.

That money goes to companies like Palo Alto, CrowdStrike and Okta.

The proof is already showing up in the numbers.

Palo Alto just reported 39% revenue growth to $3.45 billion and raised its full year forecast to as much as $14.57 billion, saying rising threats are pushing customers to buy more security.

Yesterday, as the S&P 500 fell, Okta jumped 12.1%, Palo Alto 9.9%, CrowdStrike 8%, Zscaler 6.8%, Fortinet 5.9% and Cloudflare 5.7%.

And the rally is continuing today, with $PANW up another 9.7% in pre market, $CRWD 6.5%, $NET 5.7%, $OKTA 4.5%, $ZS 4.3% and $FTNT 3.7%.

That's Palo Alto up 20.5%, Okta 17.2% and CrowdStrike 15% in just 2 days.

AI was supposed to replace these companies. Instead, it's creating more demand for them.
viral_posts.full_text_zh:

网络安全公司阻止实时攻击、保护登录并保护网络、设备和数据。像克劳德这样的人工智能工具不会这样做。

• 欧洲最大的天然气供应商Equinor 遭受网络攻击。
• 美国表示，自战争开始以来，伊朗一直在攻击美国的银行、电力和供水系统。

每一次这样的攻击都会迫使公司和政府增加安全预算。

这些资金流向 Palo Alto、CrowdStrike 和 Okta 等公司。

证据已经体现在数字中。

Palo Alto 刚刚报告收入增长 39%，达到 34.5 亿美元，并将全年预测上调至 145.7 亿美元，称不断上升的威胁正在促使客户购买更多安全产品。

昨天，随着标准普尔 500 指数下跌，Okta 上涨 12.1%，Palo Alto 上涨 9.9%，CrowdStrike 8%，Zscaler 6.8%，Fortinet 5.9% 和 Cloudflare 5.7%。

今天的涨势仍在继续，盘前 $PANW 又上涨 9.7%，$CRWD 6.5%，$NET 5.7%，$OKTA 4.5%，$ZS 4.3% 和 $FTNT 3.7%。

Palo Alto 在短短 2 天内上涨了 20.5%，Okta 上涨了 17.2%，CrowdStrike 上涨了 15%。

人工智能本来应该取代这些公司。相反，它为他们创造了更多的需求。

An AI that checks its own work is not a check. No pilot trusts a single instrument either.

Two readings disagree on the same flight. The pilot does not pick the louder one, the pilot cross-checks.

Two AI systems can check the same task and disagree, both confident, neither the sole instrument. I fly, and I follow automation closely.

@GenLayer is built for that. Validators running different AI models reach consensus on judgment calls through Optimistic Democracy, a cross-check between models, not one grading itself.

Intelligent contracts execute in GenVM on validator nodes, and validators keep the same role.

The judge did not move. The logbook did. Consensus contracts that record votes, appeals and final outcomes moved from Matter Labs' ZK Stack to @arbitrum Nitro, run by Conduit.

My test: if the judge and the logbook both stay the same, the swap should be invisible to builders.

Nitro helps there, years in production and built around Geth, so standard Ethereum tooling works as is. Robinhood launched on it in July, and more than 30 dedicated chains run the same stack.

Builders automating real tasks, when two agents disagree on whether a task is complete, which entry would you check first: votes, appeal, or final outcome?

viral_posts.full_text_en:
I estimate that within the next 5 years, you’ll be able to create a game with the level of detail and complexity of GTA VI in less than 30 days using AI.

At that stage of human-AI development, what does onchain trading and investing look like?

My prediction is that it becomes almost entirely automated and data-driven.

Trading signals, liquidity routing, and protocol selection will be determined by measurable efficacy, execution speed, capital efficiency, and optionality across strategies.

Frontends become increasingly irrelevant as AI agents interact directly with smart contracts. Much of today’s DeFi infrastructure is designed around human behavior, user interfaces, branding, and marketing.

Trading agents won’t care about your website, your KOLs, or your narrative. They’ll care about whether your protocol delivers the best execution and outcomes directly via the smart contract layer.

The competitive advantage shifts from attracting human attention to building infrastructure that autonomous agents consistently choose to use.

I’m keenly aware of this upcoming transition, and it’s something I keep in mind with every StonkBrokers product I develop on Robinhood Chain.
